articles.title: Guardians Sent Promising Youngster to Reds, and He Hit 1st MLB HR
articles.summary: Juan Brito struggled to put the pieces together for the Cleveland Guardians. Now, he’s at the other end of the state of Ohio, trying to put the pieces togeth...
articles.body:
Juan Brito struggled to put the pieces together for the Cleveland Guardians.

Now, he's at the other end of the state of Ohio, trying to put the pieces together for the Cincinnati Reds — and off to a good start.

Brito launched his first career MLB home run on Wednesday, a three-run shot in the bottom of the second inning to tie the Reds with the San Diego Padres at the time, 3-3:

Brito took his time trotting around the bases. That certainly had to feel good.

Why Did Guardians Get Rid of Juan Brito?

The Guardians had initially acquired Brito in the Nov. 2022 trade that sent Nolan Jones to the Colorado Rockies , and it looked like a good move.

Throughout his minor league career, Brito was a strong hitter. He wasn't always ready for MLB with his glove at second base, but he had enough bat to think it might not matter.

This season, the Guardians called Brito up to finally make his MLB debut, and it was brutal.

In 15 games, Brito was 9-for-51 (.176). He had four doubles and three RBI while walking four times and striking out 17 times. That was good for a rough .505 OPS.

Brito proved expendable as other young infielders showed they could play for Cleveland, and so they sent him with Alejandro Rivera in a trade on MLB deadline day to get Nathaniel Lowe from the Reds.

Lowe, at the time of the deal, was more clearly going to impact the Guardians' order the rest of this season, and they could afford to let Brito go.

Brito made his Reds debut on Sept. 1 and was 0-for-3 with a sacrifice fly for an RBI.

On Wednesday, he walked in addition to his three-run homer. The Reds went on to win that game 7-3.

The Reds improved to 67-73 with their win on Wednesday, only on the fringes of the NL Wild Card race.

A player like Brito, though, is exactly the kind of guy who can be helpful to add to the roster at this point in a season. He still has promise, even if his shine wore off a bit with his early Guardians stint.

Different teams are on different contention timelines, and the Reds can afford to wait and see what Brito can become. Maybe he rakes all September and wins himself a starting job for next year. Maybe it's a bit more touch-and-go, and there could still be questions to answer next year.

Either way, the Reds acquiring Brito gave them a chance to look into their future with a fresh face who might benefit from a change of scenery. The risk is low, and it could work out in the long run for Cincinnati.

articles.title: Former Panthers DL signs with Cardinals practice squad
articles.summary: A former Panthers defender has landed with a new team after being waived this past weekend.
articles.body:
A former Carolina Panthers defender has himself a new team.

As announced on Tuesday, the Arizona Cardinals have signed defensive end Jared Harrison-Hunte to their practice squad. The second-year lineman was waived as part of the Panthers' cutdown to their initial 53-man roster on Sunday.

Carolina signed Harrison-Hunte as an undrafted free agent in the spring of 2025, after his lone year at Southern Methodist University. The 6-foot-4, 294-pounder amassed 42 combined tackles (8.5 for a loss) and 6.5 sacks for the Mustangs en route to a first-team All-ACC selection.

Harrison-Hunte would spend much of the 2025 campaign on the Panthers' practice squad, and did not appear in a regular-season game.

The Cardinals got an up-close look at the 26-year-old back on Aug. 6, during the Hall of Fame Game. Harrison-Hunte recorded a sack of rookie quarterback Carson Beck in Carolina's 33-30 win .

articles.title: Oilers Linked to Former Senators Star Acquitted in Assault Case
articles.summary: The Edmonton Oilers are being urged to sign a former Ottawa Senators forward who was acquitted of sexual assault in 2025. The post Oilers Linked to Former Se...
articles.body:
Edmonton Oilers general manager Stan Bowman could sign a controversial player as injuries already begin to pile up. Edmonton recently announced that Mattias Janmark, Matt Savoie, Alec Regula, and Frederik Andersen would not participate in training camp later this month. The quartet is all dealing with different setbacks heading towards the new season.

While the Oilers did not get into specific details, the four players are not expected to miss significant time. Nevertheless, Edmonton has been linked to bringing in an additional NHL-ready skater, particularly at the forward position. The latest player to be named as a potential signing is Alex Formenton. The 6'2″ winger last played in the NHL for the Ottawa Senators during the 2021-22 season. He recorded 32 points on the year.

According to Edmonton Journal's David Staples, the links between the Edmonton Oilers and Formenton were made by Oilers NOW host Bob Stauffer. During a recent podcast, the team insider claimed that the winger would be a good fit with the club. "A little bit different situation, Alex Formenton," began Stauffer.

"Big rangy guy that can skate, and was a good, good penalty killer. I have a couple of friends that watched him play last year in Switzerland. Didn't think he was particularly great, but the reality is: free player."

Former NHL exec Brian Lawton agreed with Stauffer's assessment. "I would not hesitate," Lawton said of Edmonton targeting the forward. "I would want to make sure I did my due diligence, and I was comfortable with it. Alex Formenton, I could tell you, was a guy that I would be comfortable with… You're going to get what would be considered a very low-risk contract."

Edmonton Oilers may be Hesitant to Sign Alex Formenton due to Legal Battle

As Stauffer alluded to, Formenton most recently played for HC Ambrì-Piotta in Switzerland. The once highly rated forward posted 23 points, including 13 goals , in 42 games this past season. After leaving Ottawa in 2022, he has played three campaigns with the Swiss side. The winger also contributes on the penalty kill, something that the Edmonton Oilers are looking at .

Although Formenton has talent, he would be viewed as a controversial signing by many Edmonton Oilers hockey fans. The forward was one of five NHL players to be charged, and subsequently acquitted , of sexual assault. Two of the other players involved in the case, Carter Hart and Cal Foote , were targeted with fan backlash after they signed with teams following the court's ruling. It remains to be seen if the Oilers are ready to deal with a similar headache.

Edmonton Could Explore Other Forward Options

Formenton, however, is obviously not the only option for the Edmonton Oilers. Rupert McDonald of The Hockey Writers recently linked the club to several UFA forwards, including Luke Glendening and Reilly Smith. While Bowman could go in several directions, The Athletic's Allan Mitchell has regularly hinted that the Oilers would prefer to target a younger forward.

Mitchell linked Edmonton to several young forwards throughout the summer, even before the injury bug hit the Oilers. This list included Felix Unger Sörum, Matt Poitras, and Ethan Procyszyn. According to Hockey Reference , Edmonton was the eighth-oldest NHL team during the 2025-26 campaign.

articles.title: Ronald Acuña Jr. becomes fastest to 200 homers, 200 steals as Braves beat Nationals 9-0
articles.summary: Alfonso Soriano set the previous record at 929 games in August of 2006 while playing for the Nationals against the Braves.
articles.body:
Ronald Acuña Jr. hit a three-run homer to become the fastest player in major league history to reach 200 home runs and 200 stolen bases, and the Atlanta Braves beat the Washington Nationals 9-0 on Wednesday.

Sean Murphy homered for the third time in five games, a three-run shot in the sixth inning that broke a scoreless tie in a game that was interrupted by a 1-hour, 25-minute rain delay in the fourth.

Acuña followed with a drive to left-center in the seventh, his 14th of the season, to make it 6-0. He needed 904 games to reach the 200/200 club. Alfonso Soriano set the previous record at 929 games in August of 2006 while playing for the Nationals against the Braves.

Acuña stole the 225th base of his career and 20th of the season, swiping second after his leadoff single in the sixth against Riley Cornelio (2-2), who struck out the next two batters. After Michael Harris II was walked intentionally, Murphy took Cornelio deep to left.

Acuña led off the fourth with a single off Nationals starter Brad Lord. A walk and an error loaded the bases before it started raining. When play resumed, Cornelio came in and retired Murphy and Mike Yastrzemski to escape the jam.

Grant Holmes needed only 26 pitches to retire the first nine Nationals before the delay. Dylan Dodd worked a scoreless inning and Elieser Hernández (2-0) pitched the next three, allowing two hits, including James Wood's two-out single in the sixth for Washington's first hit.

Nationals catcher Keibert Ruiz left in the fourth inning after taking a foul ball off his mask.

The Braves will start LHP Chris Sale (13-9, 2.06) on Friday at Philadelphia opposite Phillies LHP Cristopher Sánchez (16-4, 2.52) in the opener of a four-game series. The Nationals begin a series at the Los Angeles Dodgers on Friday.

articles.title: ‘I’ve Been Terrible’:  Mets LHP Sean Manaea Delivers Honest Take on Late-Season Meltdown
articles.summary: Did New York Mets lefty Sean Manaea’s midseason turnaround already dissipate down the stretch? On September 1, he allowed five earned runs on 11 hits in 5.2...
articles.body:
Did New York Mets lefty Sean Manaea's midseason turnaround already dissipate down the stretch? On September 1, he allowed five earned runs on 11 hits in 5.2 innings of work. Granted, the Tampa Bay Rays are a playoff contender. Yet, that seems like an extraordinary amount of hits in less than six innings on the mound. During the postgame interview, to his credit, Manaea did not flinch in his assessment.

That appears to be an understatement, as the southpaw allowed 19 earned runs over his last 23.2 innings. That remains a far cry from his dominant 11-strikeout performance against the Pittsburgh Pirates, almost a month ago. While the Mets continue to crawl back to decency, Manaea's collapse could not take place at a more inopportune moment. While slim, a Francisco Lindor solo home run staked the veteran to a lead that he promptly surrendered.

Since the outing against the Pirates, Manaea's performances have left the Mets without an explanation. First, on August 15, against the Washington Nationals (6.1 IP, 6 H, 4 ER, 2 BB, 7 K), he didn't pitch well. The Mets ended up winning that game, but that was the last time Manaea saw the victory column.

Six days later, the AL Central-leading Chicago White Sox posted similar numbers against Manaea (6.0 IP, 5 H, 4 ER, 2 BB, 4 K) in a New York loss. Following that, losses against the Milwaukee Brewers and the Rays tell an unfortunate tale. In essence, Manaea will give six innings of work, and teammates will pepper him the second time around the order.

Another concern must center around the lack of velocity. While no one expects the left-handed batter to throw the ball by opponents every day, Manaea's game needs a sharp fastball to augment his other pitches. Without much movement, a slower heater is just that, a pitch that players can turn on and drive.

The Mets veteran looks great in the first two innings, painting the corners with velocity and accuracy. Yet, the fourth inning brings Manaea into a danger zone of sorts, one where he struggles not only to find consistency but also to maintain his command. That does not necessarily mean walks, but wild pitches in the strike zone will see batters tee off with frequency. Despite this, interim manager Andy Green still shows hope .

"I thought he battled up until the last inning. Felt good about him, in the bottom of the order. Those guys were able to spray some balls off of him. Thought it was a tough battle up until that point in time. It's been the third time through bad matchups, top of the order. Those guys did a nice job of putting the ball in play, finding grass."

The Mets continue to use the season as a developmental stage, since they remain far from rational or realistic postseason contention. Green will need to weigh Manaea's slump against the option of returning him to the bullpen, allowing a younger arm to step up. No. 1 prospect Jonah Tong continues to excel in the minors, and Manaea's spot could be the one that needs replacing.

articles.title: Giants should be ‘competitive week in and week out’, says Joe Schoen
articles.summary: Schoen assesses the roster, and talks about John Harbaugh’s impact.
articles.body:
There is tremendous optimism surrounding the New York Giants entering the 2026. They have an accomplished head coach in John Harbaugh who has raised the bar, and a roster that has been reshaped.

This, though, is a still a franchise that has won seven games combined the past two seasons, and gone 13-38 over the past three seasons.

The Giants should be better. The question is, how much better? FanDuel Sportsbook places the over/under at 7.5 wins. What is a realistic expectation?

General manager Joe Schoen was not predicting a playoff berth or setting a targeted number of victories when he spoke to media on Wednesday in his season-opening press conference. Schoen did, though, set an expectation that the product on the field would be improved.

"I feel good about the group that we have and expect us to be competitive week in and week out," the GM said. "I really like the group, both sides of the ball, special teams. The cut down was very difficult this past weekend from a depth standpoint, some difficult decisions we had to make. And even the top 70 guys in terms of the practice squad, that was difficult for us.

"Really competitive group, had a competitive camp and I like our team, I like where we are. And now really, we just got to go out and do it but I do like the roster, I like where we are. We had a competitive camp. And I'm looking forward to seeing how things go Sunday versus the Cowboys."

Harbaugh wasn't about to be dragged into making any sort of prediction.

"I know they'll go out there and be the very best football team they can be," Harbaugh said. "That's my expectation. What that ends up being depends on how good we are. And that's what you find out when you play the games, everything else is just talk."

Harbaugh does feel good about the roster the Giants have assembled in his first season in New York.

"I do, I do. I mean, I'm optimistic," Harbaugh said. "I feel good about our guys but that's always something that has to be proven. That's our mission, our mission statement is to be the best team in the National Football League and prove it because that's what it requires."

Harbaugh, a Super Bowl-winnning coach with 180 regular-season victories (14th-most all all-time) on his resume, has established a standard, pushing players hard both physically and mentally.

Schoen, in his fifth season as general manager, admitted that Harbaugh has had an impact on and off the field.

"With Coach Harbaugh, he's invested in it. He's got a passion for not just coaching and X's and O's and schemes, but the personnel part of it. So, that helps a lot. If we all have the same vision when the player gets here, it's going to be important because we're all invested in the same vision that you see it out," Schoen said. "That doesn't always happen that way. When you bring a player in and there's a vision, sometimes it can be pushed off to the side. I've got a couple different times I've seen that happen. But Coach is very invested in this, when we drafted this player, or signed this player, or hey, we got an idea, what, maybe move this player that plays center to guard, or whatever, maybe the versatility, he's typically on board with that, and he's, again, part of the process.

"He knows the league, he pays attention to players around the league, and that's helpful when you're going through the process of acquiring players, whether it be free agency or the draft. So, to me, not only is he a really good coach, he's immersed in the personnel, and he's helpful, makes us think outside the box, challenges us. And that's what has ultimately led to a lot of good conversations, communications, ultimately making the best decision for the New York Giants."

Schoen knows what to expect from Harbaugh's teams when they line up each week.

"We're going to be prepared. We're going to be prepared for the game," Schoen said. "We're going to be physical. You're going to have to go 60 minutes to compete with us. And we're going to be disciplined on both sides of the ball. And we're going to be ready to go. I know we're going to be ready to go. Week in, week out, we'll be ready."

Asked to assess how far along the Giants are in building their roster, Schoen returned to the idea that this team has enough strengths to be competitive.

"We have a young quarterback on a rookie deal, going into his second year. We've got a number one receiver in (wide receiver) Malik Nabers. Again, not to go position by position, I think we've got a strong defense, our offensive line we returned four of five starters, and the number 10 pick is being plugged in at right guard," Schoen said. "So, should be able to protect the quarterback. So, I feel good about where we are. I feel good about the roster.

"There's talent on the roster to go out and win games and be competitive week in and week out."

The Giants found themselves in the unusual position of being able to trade two offensive linemen for draft capital before trimming the roster to 53 players. They have seen a few players they released already land jobs on 53-man rosters and practice squads across the league.

That indicates league-wide recognition that Schoen isn't simply trying to talk into existence the idea that the Giants have some talent. The interest from the rest of the league in their players says so.

Schoen, though, knows there is still work to be done to bring the Giants to the top level of the NFC. The defensive line needs help. The cornerbacks appeared competent in the spring and summer, but there isn't a No. 1 guy to match up with the top receivers the Giants will face. More home-run hitting playmakers are needed on offense.

In the short term, Schoen admitted Wednesday that adding more talent at defensive tackle is a priority . The Giants will continue to try and improve the roster as much as they can during the season.

"Without getting into specifics, but we had some of these conversations this morning," Schoen said. "There are a few players out there that we are targeting or looking at, or does it make sense financially, or could we sign them? If we sign them, what's the subsequent move? And some of those positions are positions we have really good depth. Like, hey, maybe an extra, whatever it is, last man on the roster at that position, can we upgrade that?

"We're going to continue to look to upgrade everywhere we can. And so, we're still having those conversations, and we always will. If a player becomes available that'll help the roster, help the 53, and help us go win, that's what we're here for. We're always going to do that. Regardless of position, we'll try to find a way, and we'll continue to be aggressive in building the 53."

That quote was uttered by Chris Mara during a recent appearance on ESPN New York.

The view here is that the expectation should not include a run to the Super Bowl, or even the NFC Championship Game. Yet. It should include fewer games in which the Giants are not competitive. It should include enough victories, including some over good teams, that Giants fans end the season feeling good about where the team is headed.

articles.title: New York Yankees Announce Clarke Schmidt News Before Angels Series Finale
articles.summary: The New York Yankees announced news regarding right-hander Clarke Schmidt before Wednesday night's game against the Angels. The post New York Yankees Announc...
articles.body:
The New York Yankees are one step closer to getting right-hander Clarke Schmidt back.

Before Wednesday night's series finale against the Los Angeles Angels, the Yankees announced that Schmidt, who has been on the IL since undergoing Tommy John surgery last summer, had his rehab assignment moved from Double-A Somerset to Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre.

Via the New York Yankees on X: Today, the Yankees transferred the rehab assignment of RHP Clarke Schmidt from Double-A Somerset to Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre.

New York Yankees Reveal Clarke Schmidt News Before Angels Game

Schmidt faced live hitters on Aug. 4 but had to cut the session short due to forearm cramping.

The right-hander faced live hitters again late last month and felt fine enough to begin a rehab assignment on Aug, 29.

Schmidt made one appearance at Double-A before his rehab assignment was bumped to Triple-A.

In his lone Double-A outing of his current rehab stint, Schmidt allowed two runs on two hits and no walks with two strikeouts in 2/3 of an inning.

Looking at New York Yankees RHP Clarke Schmidt's Career

The Yankees selected Schmidt in the first round (No. 16 overall) of the 2017 MLB Draft out of the University of South Carolina.

Schmidt, 30, made his MLB debut with New York in 2020.

Schmidt appeared in just three games in 2020 and two games in 2021.

In 2022, Schmidt posted a 3.12 ERA with a 1.20 WHIP and 56 strikeouts in 57 2/3 innings across 29 appearances (three starts).

The Yankees converted Schmidt to a starting pitcher in 2023.

He posted a 4.64 ERA with a 1.35 WHIP and 149 strikeouts in 159 innings across 33 outings (32 starts) for New York in 2023.

In 2024, Schmidt recorded a 2.85 ERA in 85 1/3 innings across 16 starts. He missed a large chunk of the 2024 season due to a right late strain.

In 2025, Schmidt recorded a 3.32 ERA in 78 2/3 innings across 14 starts.

articles.title: Red Sox Reveal Major Garrett Crochet Rehab Update As Postseason Nears
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox have their sights set on the postseaosn, and Garrett Crochet could actually be back in time
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox are looking to make a deep run in October, and having Garrett Crochet would certainly help.

It's too late for Crochet to build back up to give the Red Sox a traditional start or go deep into a game. However, he has started playing catch and progressing toward a return. A left shoulder injury has kept him on the shelf for most of the season, but he has started throwing off a mound. The next step would be a traditional bullpen session off a mound.

Chad Tracy told reporters on Wednesday that Crochet felt good after his catch session off the mound and was up to 89-90 mph. He revealed that if Crochet is feeling good, he could throw a bullpen off the mound this weekend.

"This weekend, I think," Tracy told reporters when asked when Crochet could throw a bullpen. "We'll be gone. I'm going to check again, but that depends on how he came in today. Like, how did he feel coming off that type of intentional mound catch? We'll see how he feels, but I think the goal would be to try to get just a normal bullpen off the mound this weekend."

Tracy noted that he does not think Crochet will travel with the team this weekend as he tries to take another step toward returning.

He still has some work to do before he's ready to pitch in a game. However, if he takes too much time, there may not be any minor league games for him to rehab in. That does not mean he would not be able to return, but it would make it more difficult for the team to evaluate where his stuff is at.

It's also unclear what role he would be in if he does come back. The Red Sox could use him as an opener or a multi-inning reliever. Coming off an injury, would the team trust him late in games or in leverage spots in the postseason? He was one of the best pitchers in baseball last year, but this year has not gone his way.

He was struggling before going on the injured list, and after an injury, he may not be the same right away.

articles.title: N.J.’s Michael Zheng wins 1st main-draw match at U.S. Open
articles.summary: The former Delbarton star won’t get much rest because rain pushed his first-round match back a day
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- A huge crowd encircled Court 10 at the U.S. Open on Wednesday afternoon for the match featuring New Jersey native and former Columbia University star Michael Zheng.

His former college teammates sat in the corner of the court wearing the light blue of Columbia and cheering on the two-time former NCAA singles champion from Montville, N.J.

Competing in his first ever main-draw match at the Grand Slam in the city where he played college tennis, Zheng defeated Hungary's Fábián Marozsán, 6-4, 6-4, 6-2, to advance to the second round on Thursday.

Zheng closed it out with a forehand winner up the line for his first main-draw win at the Open. Zheng reached 124 mph on his serve and finished with 33 winners against 17 unforced errors. He won 36-of-39 points (92%) on his first serve and often followed it up with a big forehand.

The match was a rematch of their first-round encounter at the Cincinnati Open last month where Zheng beat Marozsán in three sets in the first round.

The former Delbarton star won't get much rest because rain pushed his first-round match back a day. He will next face China's Yunchaokete Bu, a Lucky Loser who stunned No. 12 seed Rafael Jodar of Spain, 6-2, 6-1, 6-1. That match is set for Court 12 not before 4 p.m. Thursday.

Zheng's win was one of several for the American men on Wednesday. No. 8 seed Ben Shelton, the top-ranked American man, advanced in four sets over Hubert Hurkacz in Arthur Ashe Stadium, while Alex Michelsen stunned No. 16 and fellow American Brandon Nakashima in straight sets on Grandstand.

It's already been quite the summer for Zheng, who reached the third round at Wimbledon before losing to No. 4 seed Felix Auger-Aliassime. He picked up nearly $250,000 in prize money at The All-England Club as a result.

After losing in U.S. Open qualifying each of the past two years, Zheng was awarded a Wild Card into the main draw this year.

In the first set, Zheng broke serve out of the rain delay for a 4-3 lead and then closed out the set on his serve for 6-4.

In the second set, Zheng got down 0-3 but broke back twice, hitting a brilliant backhand lob winner over a charging Marozsan for a 4-3 lead. He hit an inside-out crosscourt forehand winner to make it 5-3. Zheng again calmly closed out the set on his serve.

Zheng broke for 3-2 in the third set and then held easily to make it 4-2. He broke again for 5-2 before closing it out on his serve.

Columbia AD Peter Pilling was among the Columbia faithful on Court 10 and was impressed by the support for Zheng.

"Great support from the crowd," he said. "Lots of Columbia people here. Sea of Light Blue."

articles.title: Lucas Oil Retires Blue NASCAR Paint Scheme In Honor Of Kyle Busch; Changes Austin Hill’s Look
articles.summary: Another longtime NASCAR sponsor is paying tribute to the late Kyle Busch. This time, it is one of Busch’s partners at Richard Childress Racing. Just weeks af...
articles.body:
Another longtime NASCAR sponsor is paying tribute to the late Kyle Busch. This time, it is one of Busch's partners at Richard Childress Racing.

Just weeks after Joe Gibbs Racing announced M&M's will return to sponsor Ty Gibbs at Bristol Motor Speedway, a RCR sponsor will do something quite unique.

Lucas Oil, which joined Busch at RCR in 2023, was the first sponsor to go to the winner's circle after the two-time NASCAR Cup Series champion joined the team. The duo won at Auto Club Speedway in Fontana in Busch's second start with the Chevrolet-backed team. His blue, white and red paint scheme became one of his most iconic looks during his time at RCR, with the oil products firm staying on board for a handful of races with the No. 8 team each year.

This year, Busch had a chance to race his Lucas Oil scheme during the All-Star Race, and it happened to be the last time he ever competed. Now, in his memory, the firm is doing something unique.

It is extremely rare for a company that sponsors a NASCAR team to willingly change the car's look. But Lucas Oil wants the blue scheme to always be remembered for its relationship with Busch.

That is why on Wednesday afternoon, RCR and Lucas Oil announced the blue paint scheme is being retired.

The Lucas family — Morgan Lucas, CEO of Lucas Oil, and Katie Lucas, president of Lucas Oil — spoke in the video about Busch's contributions to their company, including how he helped design the now iconic paint scheme. But they are offering to bring back the blue scheme, if and when Brexton Busch would like to use it.

"For us, that iconic blue is the Busch family, and that's why we're choosing to retire the blue," the Lucas Oil president said. "Until if and when, Brexton wants it, and we will certainly save it for him. The next iteration is the red. Lucas Oil is red, white, and blue, and so, we've done the blue, and we're honored to put the red out there."

Now, Hill will sport a brand-new No. 33 Lucas Oil Chevrolet that matches the Lucas Oil red, which will remind fans of the No. 4 Lucas Oil car in the mid-2000s.

Hill will be back at RCR in 2027, a move supported by Dale Earnhardt Jr.

"Even if you don't feel like he's earned it, I think you've got to understand that this guy has been working in that building," he said. "They have created a relationship of trust and value. They just like Austin Hill and you're not gonna throw away the relationship that you have and all of the years and equity invested on the chance that you bring Josh in and it works.

"While I would've been happy that Josh Berry, as a Josh Berry fan, I would've been happy that Josh was getting an opportunity, I would've said, 'Damn, I can't believe they just cut Austin Hill. … I think they did the right thing, especially for them."

articles.title: Packers New Addition Sends Strong Message on Jordan Love
articles.summary: When the Green Bay Packers signed free agent tight end Jonnu Smith, it made plenty of sense. The team needed a tight end; he had familiarity with Matt LaFleu...
articles.body:
When the Green Bay Packers signed free agent tight end Jonnu Smith, it made plenty of sense. The team needed a tight end; he had familiarity with Matt LaFleur, and he was one of the best options available.

Still, Smith made it clear that there was more to it than that. He signed with the team because it gave him a chance to play with a strong quarterback like Jordan Love. Smith believes playing with Love was the top reason he decided to sign with the Packers when they called.

Green Bay Packers Tight End Jonnu Smith Came to Play With Jordan Love

Smith has only been with the team for a few days, and he still thinks he has seen enough to justify his decision. Smith noted that the way Love leads is mature, and he can understand why the players respond well to him.

"Very mature," said Smith on the way Love presents himself. "It's contagious in a positive way. Seeing it firsthand, seeing the kind of person he is, seeing the kind of man he is underneath the helmet."

Smith noted that the combination of being a leader in the way that Love is, combined with the player that he is, is what makes him such a special player.

Smith also played with LaFleur on the 2018 Titans, so it made things easier on all levels.

Love is the Best Quarterback Smith has Played With

Smith is entering his tenth season in the NFL . He has played with a lot of quarterbacks, but it is fair to wonder if Love is the best one that he has had. He was drafted by the Tennessee Titans and spent four seasons there. In that time, he played with Marcus Mariota, Blaine Gabbert, and Ryan Tannehill.

The next year, he signed a free-agent deal with the New England Patriots . He played with Mac Jones, Bailey Zappe, and Brian Hoyer during that two-year run.

In 2023, he signed with Arthur Smith and the Atlanta Falcons . He played with Desmond Ridder and Taylor Heinicke. The next year, he signed with the Miami Dolphins . He played with Tua Tagovailoa, Tyler Huntley, and Skylar Thompson.

Then last year, he was with the Pittsburgh Steelers . While he played with Aaron Rodgers, the Hall of Fame quarterback is not quite the player he used to be. Beyond that, Smith could not get on the same page as the veteran. He also started with Mason Rudolph at quarterback for one game.

Most of the names he has played with are not close to being considered similar to Love. So, it makes sense why Smith would want to revive his career in Green Bay after things went poorly in Pittsburgh.

Smith went from 582 yards in 2023 to 884 the following year. Then, he had just 222 yards with the Steelers. The question is whether he fell off at age 30, or whether it was just not a good fit. He seems to think that Love will help prove that he still belongs in the NFL. If so, it could be an underrated signing.

articles.title: Buccaneers Rookie Closing In on Starting Job Before Week 1
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles did not want to make a definitive statement on who the team’s starting linebacker would be next to Alex Anzalone....
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles did not want to make a definitive statement on who the team's starting linebacker would be next to Alex Anzalone. However, with a little more than a week to go until their season kicks off, he did admit that rookie Josiah Trotter is making 'a hell of a case' to be that man.

"Bowles isn't ready to commit to rookie Josiah Trotter starting at linebacker over SirVocea Dennis, but he said the rookie from Missouri is making a "hell of a case,"" tweeted Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times.

This comes after the rookie had a strong preseason and has seen his stock trend up all offseason. Meanwhile, Dennis has been in and out of the lineup with an injury.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers Rookie Linebacker Eyeing Week 1 Start

Dennis was a fifth-round pick from Pitt. He was a depth and special teams asset during his first two seasons, but the Bucs gave him a legitimate chance to start in his fourth NFL season.

Dennis started in 16 games, but things did not go too well. He played 910 snaps for the team, but had a 49.1 defensive grade, per PFF. That came with a 30.5 coverage grade. He was average in run defense with a 68.2 grade.

He allowed the fourth most yards in coverage. Dennis will be a free agent this offseason, and the team is going to start Trotter over him sooner rather than later. So, if Trotter even makes it close, it is easy to see why they would lean toward the rookie.

So far, the Missouri product has had a strong preseason.

He had been the talk of training camp and translated that to the preseason. Trotter played in just 21 snaps, but had an 80.5 PFF grade. His run defense grade was 77.4 and his coverage grade was 67.1.

Trotter came into the NFL known to be a solid downhill run defender with questions in coverage.

"He stacks backfield production with well-timed run blitzes and crafty rush work," wrote Lance Zierlein of NFL Network when he was coming out of college. "Coverage is the concern, with spotty zone awareness/spacing and the risk of being mismatched in man. Trotter's wiring and disruptive qualities make him easy to project as a productive, long-time starter in the middle, but a defense might need to protect him in coverage."

So far, he is living up to that billing. However, Dennis was already an issue in coverage as well. So, if Trotter can prove to be better in run defense and can be not as much of a liability in coverage, it is already an instant upgrade.

Between Anzalone and Trotter, the Bucs will likely have two new starters at linebacker. This is a part of their new revamped defense, which also has rookies Ruben Bain and Keionte Scott competing for playing time. Veteran defensive lineman A'Shawn Robinson has a good chance to start as well. This speaks to how much change we could see on the Bucs' defense.

articles.title: John Hunter Nemechek Breaks Silence After Legacy Departure
articles.summary: John Hunter Nemechek released a statement on his departure from Legacy Motor Club. He will not return to the No. 42 in 2027.
articles.body:
John Hunter Nemechek took to social media on Wednesday following his departure from Legacy Motor Club. On Tuesday, it was reported by Jordan Bianchi of The Athletic that Nemechek would not return to the No. 42 LMC Toyota in 2027.

After a hiatus from the NASCAR Cup Series following the 2020 season to race in the Craftsman Truck Series and O'Reilly Auto Parts Series, Nemechek returned to the Cup level in 2024 to drive the No. 42 car. Nemechek racked up four top 10s in 2024 and ranked 34th in the standings.

Improvement was seen in 2025 as Nemechek notched two top fives and eight top 10s, finishing the season 25th in the standings. After 26 races in 2026, Nemechek ranks 27th in the points and has one top five and two top 10s.

John Hunter Nemechek's statement on LMC depature

Nemechek expressed gratitude for his three seasons at Legacy Motor Club. Although he was disheartened by the organization's decision to go another way, Nemechek is driven to finish the 2026 season out strong.

On top of that, Nemechek believes his future in NASCAR remains bright.

"I am incredibly grateful to Legacy Motor Club for the past three years. While I am obviously disappointed with their decision, I am as motivated as ever. It has been such an honor to represent Toyota, Legacy Motor Club and all of their sponsors. I can't wait to continue this journey, as I know my best days are ahead."

Nemechek expressed appreciation for those closest to him and will turn his focus to the final 10 races of the 2026 season.

"This is a tough sport, and l am so thankful for the love and support from Tyler Gibbs, Jack Irving, everyone at Pye Barker, my JHN Autosports team, and so many others that have kept me lifted up through good times and bad. For now, I'm going to hug my family, focus on putting together 10 great races to finish the year, and figuring out what comes next."

Josh Berry the top candidate to take over the No. 42 in 2027

In the aftermath of Nemechek's departure, the question of who will field the No. 42 LMC Toyota in 2027 remains.

As reported by Bianchi via The Athletic , the rumor is that Josh Berry is currently the lead candidate to take over the ride next year. Berry currently pilots the No. 21 Wood Brothers Racing Ford, but is being replaced by Jesse Love after the 2026 season.

The Tennessee native has been on a hot streak over the last few races as he has posted five straight top-10 finishes, two of them being top-five results. Perhaps most impressive, Berry averaged a sixth-place finish in the month of August, the highest among any Cup Series driver.

articles.title: Diamondbacks Announce Ketel Marte News After Removal Against Phillies
articles.summary: Ketel Marte was absent from today’s lineup against the Philadelphia Phillies. The second baseman served as designated hitter in the previous two games.Philad...
articles.body:
Ketel Marte was absent from today's lineup against the Philadelphia Phillies. The second baseman served as designated hitter in the previous two games.

Philadelphia won both, 2-1 on Monday and 7-1 on Tuesday. Marte reached base multiple times, drawing a walk and collecting two singles.

On Tuesday, a pitch hit him during the sixth inning. Marte did not come out of the game and appeared fine, so Wednesday's absence is not because of that.

The Arizona Diamondbacks general manager Mike Hazen explained the move on the radio. He joined "Bickley & Marotta Mornings" on Arizona Sports 98.7 FM. Hazen said the club planned the rest day.

Arizona does not play again until Friday, when it opens a series at Houston. The Diamondbacks are off Thursday, which gives Marte two extra days of rest.

Kete Marte Injury and the Unexplained Absence

Marte's absence saga began Aug. 17 in Boston. He did not show up for that game without permission. The Diamondbacks placed him on the restricted list.

An MRI later revealed inflammation in his left knee. Arizona moved him to the 10-day injured list on Aug. 20. He received a knee injection afterward.

Pictures surfaced of him at a casino during the 9-0 win against the Cincinnati Reds . Marte did not publicly address his absence until his return.

He rejoined the team Monday for the Phillies series opener. Marte apologized to reporters and teammates before that game.

He specifically apologized to manager Torey Lovullo. "In that instance, I failed him by not showing up," Marte said through an interpreter. Chase Field fans booed Marte throughout his return Monday.

Marte is batting .251 with a .317 on-base percentage this season. His OPS sits at .761, with 21 home runs and 67 RBIs.

Torey Lovullo Believes Standings Will Shift

Arizona enters Wednesday at 73-67 this season. The Diamondbacks have lost three straight games. They trail the San Diego Padres by a half-game. It covers the final NL Wild Card spot.

Philadelphia leads the NL Wild Card standings at 79-60. They have taken 15 of their past 17 games.

Arizona used Taylor Clarke as an opener for the finale. Philadelphia countered with right-hander Andrew Painter .

Lovullo said the stretch run demands the team's best baseball. "It's September. It's the best time of the year," Lovullo said . "I think we're going to go out and play our finest month of baseball."

Lovullo also said Marte could return to second base soon. That could happen during the upcoming series at Houston. It would mark his first defensive game since the knee injury.

Right fielder Corbin Carroll has also been playing through lower back discomfort . Carroll was expected to remain in the lineup despite the issue.

articles.title: 76ers' LeBron James projected to have shocking career-low not seen in 24 years
articles.summary: Despite joining a stacked 76ers squad, LeBron James might just have one of his worst statistical years in the NBA according to ESPN projections.
articles.body:
Only one name comes to mind when longevity is talked about in the NBA - LeBron James. As he approaches the final years of his career, fans still expect a great deal of greatness and excellence from one of the greatest players of all time. However, there is a specific statistical category where he is most likely to be subpar. ESPN projected there would be a career-low year for him in one major aspect of the game, the first in 24 years. What could it be?

76ers' James projected to hit career-low points

When one thinks of LeBron James, the first record that comes to mind is his insane career total of 43,440 points. He usurped Kareem Abdul-Jabbar in the all-time record books to secure this feat and has run away with it ever since. The idea that someone could steal this record from him seems unlikely, too. To the same degree, his stint with the 76ers will mark his 24th season in the NBA. This means that he will be slowing down in major statistical categories.

The downtick everyone is looking at? James' points per game. ESPN even projects that the 76ers star will only be able to register a season average that's less than 20 points per game.

Will LeBron James average more or less than 20 points?

If the projection holds, this will mark the least amount of points James has averaged in a season. Notably, he has never scored fewer than 20 points in a season, and the 2026-27 season will likely be the first time he fails to reach that mark. Previously, his career-low in average for a season was 20.9 points. This stat line has appeared only twice in his 23-year run in the league: his last year with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2025-26 and his first season in the league with the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2003-04.

Let's look at the correlation between James' Per 36 minutes and his true points-per-game averages to see whether this bold projection has any merit. (Numbers in bold are projections)

So, why is James likely to surpass this projection by ESPN? It starts with looking at the trend in both his Per 36 and regular-season points per game. To estimate his regular-season average for 2026-27, we can multiply his Per 36 Points projection by his 33.1 average minutes from last season, then divide by 36. When the 76ers star's projected raw values are plugged in and if his scoring trend holds, he will still average about 21.1 points per game. This is still well above ESPN's projection, assuming he gets the same playing time.

Obviously, the biggest determinant in whether James can clap back statistically is whether Coach Nick Nurse gives him the touches and minutes to produce the same output. Having to share the ball with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, V.J. Edgecombe, and Jaylen Brown means the data is still volatile. James will have to morph his play style around the other 76ers stars, and that will determine whether he truly hits a career-low.

Regardless, James taking a backseat and letting the other 76ers stars do the primary work is precisely why he chose this free-agency destination. He can compete for a fifth Larry O'Brien trophy without carrying the weight of whether they succeed, unlike his stints with the Los Angeles Lakers and Cleveland Cavaliers. Even then, he might still surpass expectations, and all these bold predictions may be more wrong than ever once he pops off for the season.

articles.title: Rutgers Football Turns the Page at Kicker Ahead of 2026 Opener
articles.summary: Dane Pizzaro Named Starting Kicker Over Jai Patel One Day Before Scarlet Knights Host UMass
articles.body:
Rutgers football will have a new starting kicker in 2026.

Dane Pizzaro has won the team's kicking competition and will take over as Rutgers' starting kicker, replacing veteran Jai Patel, as first reported by Chris Iseman of the Asbury Park Press.

The decision comes just one day before Rutgers opens its 2026 season against UMass on Thursday night at SHI Stadium.

Patel, a fifth-year senior and South Brunswick native, had been Rutgers' starting kicker for the past three seasons. His sudden replacement marks one of the more notable changes to Rutgers' special teams heading into the new season.

Patel Benched Despite Storied Rutgers Career

Patel's benching is notable because of what he has accomplished during his time with the Scarlet Knights.

After joining Rutgers as a walk-on, Patel eventually earned a scholarship and established himself as one of the most reliable kickers in the program.

He set a Rutgers record with 18 consecutive made field goals, a streak that began in 2024 and continued into the 2025 season. Patel also earned Big Ten recognition during his career and has delivered several important kicks for the Scarlet Knights.

One of his biggest moments came last season at Purdue, when Patel made both the game-tying and game-winning field goals in Rutgers' 27-24 victory.

But Patel's 2025 season was not quite as consistent as his previous campaigns.

He finished the season 13-for-18 on field-goal attempts, while Rutgers also dealt with several issues in its kicking operation. Patel had five misses during a stretch of Big Ten play, including some attempts that were affected by protection problems.

That inconsistency appears to have opened the door for Pizzaro.

Pizzaro has been waiting behind Patel for his chance, after arriving in Piscataway as a preferred walk-on following his high school career at Father Judge High School in Bensalem, Pennsylvania.

He was a star soccer player in high school before switching to football in his senior year, where he played both kicker and punter. He was named First Team All-Catholic Red Division as a punter in 2024 for Father Judge.

Pizzaro has a powerful leg and showed Rutgers' coaching staff that he could be an option from long range, in addition to making two extra points against Norfolk State in relief of Patel.

That became particularly apparent last season at Minnesota.

With Rutgers trailing late and needing a 56-yard field goal to tie the game, head coach Greg Schiano elected to send Pizzaro onto the field instead of Patel.

The attempt missed wide right, but the decision itself was telling. Rutgers viewed Pizzaro as having the leg to attempt a kick from a distance that was outside Patel's typical range.

Now, Pizzaro won't just be the long-distance option.

The move gives Rutgers a younger kicker with less game experience but potentially more upside, particularly when it comes to distance.

The Timing of the Decision is Significant

The timing of Rutgers' decision to hand the job to Pizzaro is also worth watching.

On the surface, Thursday's season opener against UMass is about as favorable of an environment as Rutgers could ask for a new kicker. The Minutemen went 0-12 last season, and Rutgers enters the game as a heavy favorite at SHI Stadium.

That allows Pizzaro to settle into his new role without immediately facing the pressure of a high-stakes matchup.

But the schedule gets considerably more difficult from there.

Rutgers travels to Boston College on Sept. 11 for its first road game of the season before returning home to face USC on Sept. 19.

The Boston College game could be particularly important for Rutgers. The Scarlet Knights are expected to compete for bowl eligibility this season, and a road win over the Eagles could prove to be one of the difference-makers on that path. While RU will be favored, this would be considered a swing game for the Knights.

The Trojans represent a completely different challenge from UMass and even BC, and Rutgers will enter that matchup as a significant underdog. That means Pizzaro could have just two weeks to establish himself before facing one of the toughest opponents on the schedule.

For that reason, this decision isn't simply about who kicks against UMass.

Rutgers is betting that Pizzaro is ready to handle the position before the games become significantly more consequential.

UMass provides the runway. Boston College provides the first real test. USC could provide the first major pressure moment.

If Pizzaro handles all three, Rutgers may quickly forget about the change at kicker.

If he struggles, the decision to move on from a veteran like Patel will become a much bigger storyline.

articles.title: Oregon Ducks unveil uniform combo for Week 1 vs. Boise State
articles.summary: The Oregon Ducks have unveiled their uniforms for the Week 1 matchup against the Boise State Broncos.
articles.body:
It's been a lengthy offseason, but at long last, football is just around the corner for the Oregon Ducks. Not only does that mean that fans can go back to watching and breaking down play on the field instead of theorizing about what's to come, but it also means that one of our favorite weekly traditions in Eugene has returned as well.

On Wednesday evening, the Ducks unveiled their Week 1 jerseys for their game against the Boise State Broncos . For the season-opener, Oregon will be rocking a green and yellow look, with yellow helmets, a green top, and yellow pants.

This look is similar to what we saw last year against the Montana State Bobcats in Week 1, but with a yellow helmet that has the Oregon "O" on the side, rather than the green wings.

While the uniform combo for this first game against Boise State is relatively tame compared to Oregon's standards, there is an early expectation that a couple of games will get some special jersey treatment in Eugene. Earlier this year, at Big Ten Media Days, tight end Jamari Johnson dropped a hint that the uniforms in Week 4 against the USC Trojans, and the final week of the year against the Washington Huskies, are going to be special.

While we wait to see what those are, here's a closer look at what Oregon will be wearing this week against Boise State:

articles.title: Which young player are you most excited to watch this season?
articles.summary: After training camp and preseason, which young player are you most excited to watch this season?
articles.body:
We are on the literal cusp of Week 1 of the 2026 regular season in the NFL. It's been a looooong wait, Broncos Country, but the wait is finally almost over. Given that we've had a full training camp and three preseason games, we thought the best question to ask in our weekly fan survey was to highlight the young player you are most excited to watch this season. Vote below and we'll come back with some neat graphics later on in the week!

Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Broncos fans and fans across the country.
